newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macmahon forecasts A$23.8 mln profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macmahon forecasts A$23.8 mln profit.

text.p: Macmahon Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday in a prospectus for its converting preference share issue that it forecast pre-tax operating profit would rise to A$23.8 million in the year to June 30, 1997 from A$15.74 million in 1995/96.

"The company's before tax profit growth - which included a 78 percent jump from A$8.8 million to A$15.74 million in the past financial year - is forecast to improve further to approximately A$23.8 million in 1996/97," Macmahon said.

Macmahon chief executive Graeme Beissel said the outlook for the contract mining sector generally remained strong with major new mining-related infrastructure projects already underway or planned throughout Australia and in South East Asia.

"We have started the new financial year with a record forward order book and with good prospects for winning additional new contracts throughout Australia and in Asia during the new financial year," he said.
Macmahon said earlier on Tuesday it planned a converting preference share issue to raise A$44 million.

Each converting preference share would convert into one ordinary share on November 15, 2000 and, subject to market conditions, a bonus issue of one share per converting preference would be made, Macmahon said.

The issue was being underwritten by Macquarie Underwriting and 34 million of the 44 million shares being issued at A$1 per share would be offered to Macquarie clients. The remaining 10 million shares would be offered to Macmahon shareholders.
Macmahon shares were up one cent at 89 cents at 12.20 p.m. (0220 GMT).
